reader.requirement: At --std 85 the UNSTRING POINTER operand identifier-7 must be an elementary numeric integer item with no P in its PICTURE, large enough to hold 1 plus the size of identifier-1; any other description (non-integer, P-scaled, alphanumeric, numeric-edited, group, too few digits for 1 + size of the sender, including the maximum size of a variable-length sender) is refused.

reader.notes: One edition-blind screen in BindUnstring: StrUnstrIsInteger (elementary unscaled integer, asked of the operand as bound) then PointerTooSmall (compile-time size of identifier-1, ODO maximum included). The 1985 text and the 2023 SR6 state the same rule, so one arm is right for both. The diagnostic cites §2023:14.9.48.3 SR6 at --std 85 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: Read StringUnstringBinder.cs#BindUnstring pointer arm, #StrUnstrIsInteger (operand as bound, IsUnscaledInteger) and #PointerTooSmall (compile-time size incl. group size). Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-223/src): ux1 USAGE INDEX pointer -> COBOL1651 'shall be an elementary numeric integer data item' (an index item has no PICTURE, so refusal is right); ux2 group sender of 98 bytes with PIC 99 pointer accepted, group of 99 bytes -> COBOL1651 too small (1+99=100); ux3 66 RENAMES of one elementary PIC 99 item accepted, A=CD RP=07; ux4 FUNCTION LENGTH(SRC) as identifier-7 -> COBOL5506 parse refusal; ux5 binary PIC 99 COMP and S9(3)V SIGN LEADING SEPARATE pointers accepted, A=CD PN=07 / PD=+007.
